text: This is the model Finance and Ops will both query, built with the same materialized incremental and is_incremental idiom this project's own earlier lesson already teaches — applied for real this time.

Two refs in, orders joined to payments for the first time, and the is_incremental block at the end: false on the first run, building everything, true after that, filtering on order_date against the max already in this table.
Order_date is this model's watermark — it reliably increases and is populated on every row. Unique_key is order_id, so a rerun updates a row that changed instead of duplicating it.

This is the first model to bring in payments. Watch the row count after adding this join. If it's larger than int_orders__joined's row count, something about this join isn't one-row-per-order. Note that observation — don't fix anything yet.
Next lesson: writing a custom Jinja macro — a reusable cents_to_dollars helper, because payments.amount in the real jaffle shop data is stored in cents.
